Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

r4subtrace (development version)

  • Add validate_trace_graph(), structural integrity checks on the derivation graph behind trace_chains(). It returns a tidy diagnostic report that flags circular derivation chains (strongly connected components), dangling edges (a derivation that names a variable not in the model), orphan nodes (a variable in no derivation edge), and disconnected components (a group of derivations with no SDTM source). Purely structural graph checks, found with standard algorithms; no trace level, coverage, or score is involved.
  • Add trace_lineage(), a path query over the same graph. Given one variable it returns either its full upstream ancestry (every source it derives from, down to SDTM) or its downstream dependents, each at its shortest distance with a readable path reading outward from the variable. trace_impact() is the downstream-of-a-source special case; trace_lineage() generalizes it to either direction from any node. Circular references are handled.
  • Add export_trace_graph(), which serializes the derivation graph behind trace_chains() to a portable text format: Graphviz DOT, Mermaid, or GraphML. Unlike plot_trace_graph(), which needs igraph and only renders interactively, the text can be committed to version control, embedded in an ADRG or vignette, rendered by Graphviz, or opened in a graph editor. Edges run from a derived variable to its source, ADaM-to-ADaM derivations are included when supplied, and every variable node is emitted so orphans and unused SDTM sources show as isolated nodes. Pure serialization: trace levels, coverage, and scoring are unchanged.
  • Complete the pkgdown reference index with sdtm_utilization(), summarize_impact(), and export_impact_report(), which were exported but missing from the documentation site index.
  • Add export_impact_report() and summarize_impact(), which turn the result of trace_impact() into reportable form. summarize_impact() prints a short digest and rolls up the affected downstream variables by dataset and by level (distance from the change); export_impact_report() writes the full affected list, with paths and the changed variable, to a data.frame, CSV, or Excel file for a change-control record. Reporting only: trace_impact() and the derivation graph are unchanged.
  • Add sdtm_utilization(), the mirror image of orphan detection. Given a trace model, it reports which SDTM source variables are referenced by no ADaM variable, the dead or unused sources in a submission, with a per-variable used-count. It reuses the same reverse adjacency as trace_impact() and is a pure diagnostic: trace levels, coverage, and scoring are unchanged.
  • Import %||% from rlang explicitly. It was used in trace_model_to_evidence() but relied on the base R %||%, which only exists from R 4.4.0, so evidence emission could fail on the R 4.2/4.3 versions the package still declares support for. No change to traceability behavior.

r4subtrace 0.3.1

  • Complete the pkgdown reference index so the documentation site builds, and polish metadata for CRAN.

r4subtrace 0.3.0

  • Add trace_impact(), impact analysis for a changed source variable. Given a variable that is about to change, it walks the derivation graph in reverse and returns every ADaM variable that derives from it, directly or through a chain, each with its distance from the change and a readable path back to it. This is the question a data team asks before editing a source: what breaks downstream. Circular references are handled and multi-step chains are followed through adam_derivations, the same input trace_chains() uses.

r4subtrace 0.2.1

  • Add trace_problems(), a focused view of just the traceability issues worth acting on: variables that are not traced to the required level, and, when a derivation table is supplied, chains that never reach SDTM, that are circular, or that were cut off at the depth limit. On a large submission this is what a team consumes rather than the full per-variable coverage table. The engine is verified on a 10,000-variable synthetic model.

r4subtrace 0.2.0

  • Add export_traceability_report() and traceability_coverage(), which summarize traceability coverage per ADaM dataset (percent traced, untraced variables listed) with an overall summary row, and export the table as a data.frame, CSV, or Excel file for ADRG appendices.
  • Add trace_chains(), which follows multi-step derivation chains back to source (ADaM derived from ADaM derived from SDTM), reports the depth and whether each variable is grounded in SDTM, caps the walk with trace_depth, and detects circular references. Add plot_trace_graph() to draw the derivation graph with igraph.
  • Add vignette: “Case study: tracing ADaM back to SDTM”, a worked walkthrough building a trace model from the example CDISC pilot metadata in r4subdata, finding orphan variables, and reading the coverage indicators.
  • Clarified the package DESCRIPTION: “R4SUB” expands to “Ready for Submission” (previously “R for Regulatory Submission”, inconsistent with the rest of the ecosystem).

r4subtrace 0.1.1

  • Add vignette: “Traceability Analysis with r4subtrace” covering build_trace_model(), compute_trace_levels(), trace_indicator_scores(), and orphan variable detection.
